case.inventionTitle: INTERACTIVE ELECTRONIC GREETING CARDS WITH TAP AND TOUCH ACTIVATED EFFECTS

timeline.message: I've filed a patent application for INTERACTIVE ELECTRONIC GREETING CARDS WITH TAP AND TOUCH ACTIVATED EFFECTS.

The invention is an interactive greeting card featuring an internal electronics module that plays multiple digital audio files. It utilizes a slide switch to initiate playback upon opening the card and a touch-sensitive mechanism that triggers additional audio content based on specific physical interactions, such as tapping or a continuous back-and-forth motion.
The application is complete and has been accepted for examination.
The application has been published.

The invention is an interactive greeting card featuring an internal electronics module that utilizes multiple digital audio files stored on a memory device. These files are triggered by a combination of switches, including touch-sensitive sensors and slide mechanisms, to provide specific audio content or verbal instructions to the user. The card design incorporates printed indicia and specific physical interactions, such as back-and-forth motions or unfolding panels, to create an immersive, responsive multimedia experience.

timeline.description: Applicant Arguments/Remarks Made in an Amendment
timeline.message: In response to the office action, I have provided the requested remarks for your consideration regarding application number 13/090,569. Should you have any questions or wish to discuss these points in greater detail, please feel free to contact me via telephone at your earliest convenience.

The claims in this application are directed to patentably distinct species of switches, which require different searches and examinations. Please elect a single species or grouping of patentably indistinct species for prosecution on the merits, while identifying the claims readable on your chosen election. Your response must be received within the set time period to avoid abandonment.
I've responded to the restriction requirement with an election.

timeline.description: Applicant Arguments/Remarks Made in an Amendment
timeline.message: I respectfully elect to proceed with Group IV, covering claims 1–15 and 17–20, while requesting the cancellation of claims 16, 21, and 22. Please charge any associated fees to Deposit Account No. 50-0959 and contact me if any further matters require discussion.

This non-final action includes objections to the drawings and a requirement for election of species for claims 16, 21, and 22. Furthermore, claims 1-7 are rejected for indefiniteness under 35 U.S.C. 112, and various claims are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over the cited prior art.
I've filed an amendment in response to the non-final rejection.

The invention has been refined to focus on interactive greeting cards that utilize specific physical interactions to control digital audio playback. These updates clarify that audio playback is tied to continuous user input—such as back-and-forth rubbing motions—and define how these motions can modulate volume, playback speed, or resume functions from a paused state.

timeline.description: Applicant Arguments/Remarks Made in an Amendment
timeline.message: I have submitted amendments to claims 1, 8, 15, and 17–19 to address concerns regarding indefiniteness and to clarify that our interactive greeting card requires continuous user motion for audio playback. I respectfully request the withdrawal of the rejections and the issuance of a Notice of Allowance, as the cited prior art does not teach or suggest these specific interactive features.

This Office action is made final, as your recent amendments have necessitated new grounds of rejection. The application remains rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112 for lack of antecedent basis and under 35 U.S.C. § 103 for obviousness, and the drawings are objected to for failing to show all claimed features.
I've filed a response to the final rejection.

The invention is an interactive greeting card featuring an internal electronics module that plays back multiple digital audio files based on specific user interactions. The current claims define a device where audio playback is strictly tied to continuous user input—such as persistent pressure, specific rubbing motions, or back-and-forth movements—ensuring that audio ceases immediately when the interaction stops. Furthermore, the invention incorporates features that allow the speed of the user's motion to dynamically control the playback volume or tempo of the audio files.

timeline.description: Applicant Arguments/Remarks Made in an Amendment
timeline.message: I have submitted amendments to address the indefiniteness rejections by clarifying claim language and providing proper antecedent basis. Additionally, I contend that the 35 U.S.C. § 103 rejections are improper because the cited prior art is not analogous and fails to teach the novel, user-interactive audio controls unique to my greeting card invention. Accordingly, I respectfully request the withdrawal of all rejections and the allowance of the pending claims.
I've filed a Request for Continued Examination.

timeline.description: Amendment Submitted/Entered with Filing of Continued Prosecution Application (CPA)/Request for Continued Examination(RCE)
timeline.message: I've submitted claim amendments with the Request for Continued Examination.

The invention is an interactive greeting card featuring an internal electronics module that enables audio playback through specific user interactions, such as continuous back-and-forth rubbing motions on designated card areas. Recent amendments refine these interactions by specifying that the speed and volume of the audio playback are dynamically controlled by the velocity of the user’s physical input. This design ensures that audio is tied directly to user activity, pausing immediately when the motion stops and resuming from that point if the interaction is re-initiated.

timeline.description: Applicant Arguments/Remarks Made in an Amendment
timeline.message: I have amended claims 1, 7, 8, 15, and 18 to incorporate the subject matter previously accepted by the Examiner and to clarify their patentability. Given these adjustments and the cancellation of claims 10 and 11, I believe the remaining claims are now in condition for allowance. I respectfully request a Notice of Allowance and remain available by telephone should you wish to discuss these amendments further.

The finality of the previous Office action has been withdrawn following your Request for Continued Examination. Claims 1-6 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103, while claims 8, 9, and 12-19 are currently allowed.
I've filed an amendment in response to the non-final rejection.

The invention features an interactive greeting card that utilizes an internal electronics module to control digital audio playback based on user interaction. Specifically, the system is designed to modulate both the speed and volume of the audio output in direct response to the speed of a continuous back-and-forth rubbing motion applied to a specific area of the card.

timeline.description: Applicant Arguments/Remarks Made in an Amendment
timeline.message: I have amended claim 1 to incorporate the limitations of previously cancelled claim 7 to overcome the Examiner’s 103(a) rejections. I respectfully request that the Examiner withdraw these rejections and issue a Notice of Allowance for the pending claims, as they are now in condition for allowance.

timeline.description: Notice of Allowance and Fees Due (PTOL-85)
timeline.message: The application has been allowed. Once the issue fee is paid, the patent will be granted.
The patent will issue as U.S. Patent No. 8584385.
